title: Longest Block of Frequent Letters

concept.title: A rare letter can never be inside the answer
body: You want the longest block in which **every letter that occurs appears at least `k` times**. Count the letters of the whole word. If every letter has a count of at least `k`, the whole word is the answer. Otherwise there is a letter with fewer than `k` occurrences in total, and **no valid block can contain it** (a block has even fewer of them). So cut the word at every occurrence of such rare letters and solve each piece separately.

body.code:
def best(lo, hi):
    count the letters of s[lo:hi]
    if no letter has 0 < count < k: return hi - lo
    split at every letter with count < k, return the max of best(piece) over the pieces

body: Each recursion level removes at least one of the 26 letters from consideration, so the depth is at most 26 and each level reads the word once: O(26 * n) in total.

statement: Given a word and a number `k`, find the length of the longest block of consecutive letters in which every letter that appears in the block appears at least `k` times. If there is no such block, print 0.
inputFormat: The second line has the word.

examples.note: The block aaa (b appears only twice).
The block ababb: a appears 2 times and b 3 times.

hints: If every letter of the word appears at least k times, the whole word is the answer.
A letter with fewer than k occurrences in the word cannot be in any valid block.
Split the word at those letters and solve the pieces recursively.

solution.complexity: Time O(26 * n), space O(26) recursion depth.
